arguments.text: Fixed (Request #1). In src/plugin/timezone/index.js, `dayjs.tz(input, tz)` fed every input through `d.utc(input)`, so a timestamp / js Date / Day.js object was parsed as a local wall-clock string. Added the missing non-string branch: `if (typeof input !== 'string') return d(input).tz(timezone)`. `Parse parse timestamp, js Date, Day.js object` now gives 2014-06-01T12:00:00-04:00 / 1401638400000 / offset -240 for all three input kinds. Full suite re-run in UTC/Auckland/London/Whitehorse: no pre-existing green test broken.

Fixed (Request #2). In src/plugin/timezone/index.js, `proto.tz` computed `diff = (this.toDate() - new Date(target)) / 1000 / 60` without rounding; when the source instant had non-zero milliseconds the offset became fractional (e.g. -240.00205), so `format('Z')` produced garbage like "-04:0.00205…". Wrapped it in `Math.round(...)`; `Convert format Z` now yields "-04:00"/"-0400"/"+09:00" etc. for `dayjs()`, `dayjs(new Date())` and ms-carrying inputs. No pre-existing green test broken (verified in all 4 test timezones).

Fixed (Request #3). src/locale/nl.js had `ordinal: n => `${n}.``, which is not the Dutch ordinal and disagrees with moment's nl locale. Replaced with the Dutch rule (1ste, 2de, …, 8ste, …, 19de, 20ste, … 31ste), bracket-wrapped so the suffix is not re-parsed as format tokens: `ordinal: (n) => { const s = ['ste', 'de']; return `[${n}${n === 1 || n === 8 || n >= 20 ? s[0] : s[1]}]` }`. `Format Day of Month Do 1 - 31` now matches moment for all 31 days; test/locale/keys.test.js still passes.

Fixed (Request #4). src/plugin/weekYear/index.js only handled "week 1 in December → year+1" and was missing the mirror case: early January that still belongs to the previous week-year. Added `if (month === 0 && weekOfYear >= 52) return year - 1`. With a yearStart: 4 locale (en-gb), e.g. 2016-01-01/02/03 now return 2015, matching moment; the existing weekYear/weekOfYear tests still pass.

Fixed (Request #5). src/plugin/customParseFormat/index.js parsed the A/a tokens with the hard-coded regexes /[AP]M/ and /[ap]m/ and compared the text to the literal 'PM'/'pm', so locale meridiems could not be parsed at all. Added a `meridiemMatch(input, isLowerCase)` helper that falls back to the literal AM/PM when the locale has no `meridiem`, and otherwise matches the input against `locale.meridiem(i, 0, isLowerCase)` for i = 1..24 (afternoon when i > 12); A/a now use the generic `matchWord` regex. `meridiem locale AM`/`PM` ('2018-05-02 01:02:03 上午'/'下午' with zh-cn) now equal moment's values (1525222923000 / 1525266123000). All 38 existing customParseFormat tests still pass.

Fixed (Request #6). src/plugin/duration/index.js's `unitToMS` map had no `milliseconds` entry, so `dayjs.duration(1, 'milliseconds')`/`('ms')` multiplied by undefined and produced an invalid duration (toISOString() 'P0D', asMilliseconds() NaN, add/subtract NaN). Added `milliseconds: MILLISECONDS_A_SECOND / 1000`. `Creating milliseconds` now works: duration(1,'ms').toISOString() === 'PT0.001S', duration(100,'milliseconds') === 'PT0.1S', asMilliseconds()/milliseconds()/add() correct; the existing duration suite (14 tests) still passes.
